*** Add File: {{workspace:people/maya-desai}}/knowledge/people/maya-desai/onboarding-plan.md
+# Maya Desai — Senior Platform Engineer onboarding plan
+
+Status: **isolated pending access approval**  
+Manager: Ethan Park, Engineering Manager, Platform Control Plane  
+Team lead / escalation: Priya Natarajan, VP Engineering, Platform  
+Scope: LiteLLM gateway and Langfuse operations-console work
+
+## Role boundaries
+
+Maya may design, implement, test, and document changes to inference-gateway policy, tenant configuration, safe rollout controls, telemetry workflows, and the operator-facing console. The team uses LiteLLM for gateway work and Langfuse for observability and console workflows. She should coordinate, not unilaterally decide, where changes touch product behavior, security boundaries, billing/metering, runtime behavior, SRE-owned production controls, or release policy. [E1]
+
+Ethan owns Maya's management and the Platform Control Plane boundary (customer configuration, policy evaluation, auth integration points, and reliability). Priya is the Platform engineering lead. Dylan Brooks owns Console & Tooling; Chloe Martin owns Console Backend; Logan Wright owns Telemetry & Analytics; Mina Haddad owns Smart Routing. [E2]
+
+## First week: access and local setup
+
+All access is least-privilege and approval-gated. Until approvals below are recorded, use the isolated knowledge branch, local fixtures, mock tenants, and non-production test data only.
+
+1. Confirm managed device, SSO/MFA, security training, source-control identity, and signed contributor requirements with People Ops/IT.
+2. Request read access first for the LiteLLM and Langfuse mirrors, Platform & Console documentation, issue tracker, CI results, and non-production observability. Request write/merge permissions separately.
+3. Ethan approves team/repository scope; the repository/code owner approves write or merge rights; Cloud Infra approval is required for production-level access. People Ops and Ethan resolve delayed onboarding access. [E3]
+4. Clone the company-approved pinned mirrors only after repository access is approved. Follow each repository's checked-in contributor instructions; do not copy secrets into shell history, config files, fixtures, traces, screenshots, or issues.
+5. Build and test with synthetic data. Start LiteLLM gateway/proxy tests and a Langfuse local console stack; validate a synthetic request produces a trace visible in the local UI. Do not connect a local stack to customer or production endpoints.
+6. Read the team brief, architecture/codebase map, recent release notes, representative postmortems, API contracts, and SLOs. Shadow an on-call handoff but do not join the production rotation in week one. [E1][E3]
+7. Deliver a small documentation or test-only change and a short end-of-week walkthrough. Validation: lint/unit tests pass, no secret or customer-data findings, mentor review complete, and no production deployment.
+
+## Repository ownership and review routing
+
+- LiteLLM gateway: Ethan is accountable for control-plane integration. Amara Diallo is the API-gateway specialist; Kaitlyn Nguyen reviews authn/authz and tenant-isolation implications; Cole Summers reviews quota/billing-hook changes; Mina Haddad or Ravi Menon reviews routing/fallback behavior. [E2]
+- Langfuse operations console: Dylan is accountable for Console & Tooling; Chloe owns Console Backend. Jada Williams is the staff-level console architecture reviewer; Logan Wright owns telemetry/analytics, with Nadia Rahman for metering and Caleb Johnson for trace/metrics ingestion. [E2]
+- Release and production controls: Connor O'Brien coordinates release trains; SRE owns on-call and production reliability controls. Security and the relevant code owner must approve boundary-changing work. [E2]
+
+## Safe handling of upstream issues
+
+Treat LiteLLM and Langfuse as upstream-first dependencies:
+
+1. Reproduce against Redwood's pinned source revision with a minimal, sanitized evidence artifact.
+2. Separate three questions in the triage note: upstream behavior, Redwood compatibility policy, and immediate incident mitigation.
+3. Link an upstream issue or contribution. Do not disclose customer identifiers, payloads, credentials, topology, private logs, or Redwood-only security details.
+4. Prefer an upstreamable minimal fix. A downstream patch is temporary and allowed only when an operational boundary requires containment.
+5. Before rollout, record owner, scope, tests, removal condition, rollback criteria, and upstream link. Validate in local/test and then staging; production promotion requires the normal owner, security/reliability, and release approvals.
+6. Remove the downstream patch after the pinned upstream version contains the qualified fix and regression tests pass. [E4][E5]
+
+## First 30 days
+
+### Days 1–5 — orient and prove the local path
+
+- Complete approved read access and local synthetic LiteLLM → Langfuse flow.
+- Pair with Benji Okafor on control-plane/safe-rollout primitives and with Jada Williams or Felix Schneider on console workflows.
+- Shadow support/on-call triage; publish one reviewed runbook or test improvement.
+
+### Days 6–10 — bounded issue qualification
+
+- Select one non-sensitive support or upstream issue with Ethan.
+- Produce a pinned-version reproduction, minimal fixture, ownership classification, and proposed validation matrix.
+- Review gateway impact with Amara/Kaitlyn as applicable and console/telemetry impact with Chloe/Logan as applicable.
+
+### Days 11–20 — implement safely
+
+- Implement a small fix or observability improvement behind a test/staging boundary.
+- Add unit/integration coverage, compatibility notes, and explicit rollback/removal criteria.
+- Obtain code-owner review and demonstrate the result in staging; do not self-approve or self-promote.
+
+### Days 21–30 — close the loop
+
+- Complete a second, slightly broader cross-subsystem change or an upstream contribution.
+- Update the codebase map/runbook from learned facts.
+- Hold a 30-day review with Ethan: readiness score, blockers, mentor feedback, two next priorities, and whether any additional access is justified. [E3]
+
+## Mentors, approvers, and escalation
+
+- Manager and primary onboarding owner: Ethan Park.
+- Executive/team escalation and Platform boundary: Priya Natarajan.
+- Gateway mentors: Benji Okafor (control plane/safe rollout), Amara Diallo (gateway), Kaitlyn Nguyen (auth/tenant isolation).
+- Console mentors: Jada Williams (architecture), Felix Schneider (dashboards/audit), Chloe Martin (backend manager).
+- Telemetry mentor: Caleb Johnson; escalate metering/cost attribution to Nadia Rahman and Logan Wright.
+- Release approver: Connor O'Brien. Production reliability approval: the owning SRE/Cloud Infra authority. Security approval is required for auth, secrets, tenant boundaries, KMS, or sensitive telemetry.
+
+## Validation and approval gates
+
+- Access: recorded manager + system/repository owner approval; Cloud Infra approval for production. No approval is implied by this document. [E3]
+- Change: issue/reproduction linked; affected owners named; tests green; sanitized evidence; rollback/removal criteria; upstream link where relevant. [E4][E5]
+- Staging: synthetic test passes end to end; telemetry cardinality and tenant scoping checked; console behavior smoke-tested.
+- Production: explicit release, code-owner, reliability, and security approvals; canary/hold point and rollback path documented. Maya does not self-approve.
+
+## Current approval gaps
+
+- Maya is not present in the authoritative employee directory snapshot, so reporting-line and employment activation need confirmation. [E2]
+- No authoritative record retrieved grants Maya repository, CI, issue-tracker, non-production observability, secrets, console-admin, or production access.
+- LiteLLM/Langfuse mirror revisions, exact local bootstrap commands, CODEOWNERS groups, and required CI checks must be confirmed after read access; they are intentionally not invented here.
+- Named mentors are proposed from authoritative role ownership; Ethan and each mentor must confirm availability.
+- Production, customer-data, secrets/KMS, and incident-command privileges remain unrequested/unapproved.
+
+## Evidence
+
+- [E1] `curated_024986ded9ae947c8913f2eb`, `/knowledge/curated/team-platform-console/brief.md` — team scope, source areas, tools, and lead.
+- [E2] `enterprise_9fbbe916a1d8961396219789`, `/knowledge/company/employee_directory.yaml` — organization, managers, and role ownership.
+- [E3] `dsid_f954519b2b004d20acf952719135340a`, `/knowledge/company/sources/confluence/company-handbook/04_hiring-and-onboarding/embedded-onboarding-playbook-for-product-and-platform-teams-2026.json` — first-week setup, staged access, validation, and production approval.
+- [E4] `infra_b0bb081732d3f8b2ab8b16f16d248328`, `/knowledge/company/sources/github/redwood/infra-v1-github-004.json` — pinned reproduction, upstream-first/downstream-patch rules, rollback and upstream-link review requirements.
+- [E5] `infra_94ddb96e68610aa0f35d5b6a2d77276f`, `/knowledge/company/sources/gmail/aditya_rao/infra-v1-gmail-017.json` — Langfuse qualification decision and reviewer checklist.

*** Add File: {{workspace:people/maya-desai}}/knowledge/teams/platform-console/codebase-map.md
+# Platform & Console codebase map
+
+This map connects the upstream codebases to Redwood accountability. Paths are functional areas, not a grant of access or a substitute for repository CODEOWNERS. Confirm exact paths and required checks in the pinned mirror after access approval.
+
+## System boundary
+
+Request/config path: Console workflow → control-plane policy/config → LiteLLM gateway → model/provider.  
+Operational evidence path: LiteLLM request outcome → tracing/metrics ingestion → Langfuse analytics/console → operator decision and safe rollout.
+
+The Platform & Console team owns gateway policy, tenant configuration, safe rollouts, telemetry workflows, and the operator-facing console. LiteLLM is the gateway dependency; Langfuse supports observability and console workflows. Product, security, SRE, release engineering, routing, and billing retain their specialist boundaries. [E1]
+
+## LiteLLM gateway
+
+| Subsystem | Redwood responsible roles | Review / escalation boundary |
+|---|---|---|
+| Proxy/API entry points, request validation, provider contract | Ethan Park (accountable); Amara Diallo (API gateway); Brian Murphy (API ergonomics) | Security for externally visible/auth changes; Runtime for provider/runtime-contract changes |
+| Authentication, authorization, keys, tenant isolation | Ethan Park; Kaitlyn Nguyen; Ines Carvalho | Security approval required; never use customer credentials in tests |
+| Policy/config persistence, migrations, rollout primitives | Ethan Park; Benji Okafor; Jordan Lee; Michael Nguyen | Console workflow review by Chloe/Jada; rollback and migration plan required |
+| Routing, fallback, regional/tier behavior | Mina Haddad; Ravi Menon; Elena Popov; Zachary Hill | SRE for failover/circuit breakers; Product for customer-visible semantics |
+| Rate limits, quotas, usage enforcement, billing hooks | Cole Summers; Nadia Rahman for metering | Finance/billing and telemetry data-quality review |
+| Gateway performance and data-plane connectivity | Amara Diallo; Vikram Singh | Runtime/SRE review for latency, overload, or fleet effects |
+
+## Langfuse operations console
+
+| Subsystem | Redwood responsible roles | Review / escalation boundary |
+|---|---|---|
+| Console backend, dashboards, enterprise admin | Dylan Brooks (accountable for Console & Tooling); Chloe Martin (manager); Jada Williams (staff architecture) | Product review for UX/semantics; Security for admin or tenant scope |
+| Rollout/A-B workflows, notifications, rollback UI | Jada Williams; Hannah Rivera; Jin Woo Park | Control Plane owner for policy execution; Release Engineering/SRE for promotion |
+| Audit, status, error-analysis, observability links | Felix Schneider; Nora Ahmed; Svetlana Petrenko | Security/privacy for audit/export; Support for operator workflows |
+| Trace and metrics ingestion/data quality | Logan Wright (accountable); Caleb Johnson; Thomas Baird | SRE for operational signals; cardinality/retention and tenant isolation checks |
+| Metering, cost attribution, analytics datasets | Nadia Rahman; Mei Lin | Billing/Finance and data governance review |
+| End-to-end validation and release automation | Leila Farouk; Devon Price; Connor O'Brien | Required checks, reproducible release, staged/canary rollout |
+
+## Cross-subsystem triage ownership
+
+- Missing/incorrect gateway response before trace creation: start with Amara/Ethan; involve provider/runtime owner.
+- Correct gateway outcome but missing or malformed trace: start with Caleb/Logan; check serialization, ingestion, tenant scope, and cardinality.
+- Correct stored trace but incorrect/missing UI presentation: start with Chloe/Jada/Felix; verify stable vs preview behavior and API/UI contracts.
+- Wrong quota/cost display: Cole + Nadia, then Console; do not patch the display to hide source-data errors.
+- Routing/fallback mismatch shown in Console: Mina/Ravi own policy semantics; Ethan owns config/control-plane integration; Console owns presentation.
+- Production incident: SRE incident command owns containment. Component owners supply reproduction and rollback; upstream work follows the upstream-first procedure. [E2][E3]
+
+## Qualification and contribution rule
+
+For both dependencies, reproduce on the pinned source revision, attach a minimal sanitized artifact, distinguish upstream behavior from Redwood policy and mitigation, and link the upstream issue/contribution. Downstream patches are temporary operational exceptions with an owner, removal condition, tests, and rollback criteria. [E3][E4]

arguments.summary: For Platform & Console hires working on LiteLLM and Langfuse: begin with an isolated personal knowledge branch and least-privilege read access; keep local work synthetic and non-production until recorded approvals. The manager approves team scope, repository/code owners approve write/merge, and Cloud Infra plus relevant security/reliability authorities approve production-level access. Route gateway changes through Platform Control Plane/API Gateway and affected auth, routing, quota, telemetry, or runtime owners; route console changes through Console Backend/Tooling and affected telemetry/product/security owners. For upstream issues, reproduce against the pinned revision with a minimal sanitized artifact, separate upstream behavior from Redwood compatibility policy and incident mitigation, link an upstream issue or contribution, and use a downstream patch only as a temporary operational exception. Before staging or production, record owner, tests, removal condition, rollback criteria, and required code-owner/security/reliability/release approvals. New hires do not self-approve or self-promote.
